cli.result:
I converted 568 of the 678 locators and skipped 110 with reasons. I couldn't test any of the chains: there was no shell, so nothing was run against WDA or a device. The JSON has not been parsed or validated. I only read the files back and confirmed each part ends at the expected id.

The result is in `output-1.json` to `output-12.json` in the working folder. Parts 1–11 hold 60 ids each (x001–x660) and part 12 holds x661–x678. I did not write an `output.json`, so the merge won't see duplicates.

## What I skipped (110)
- **Sibling, following, parent and ancestor steps** (`following-sibling::`, `preceding-sibling::`, `following::`, `..`, `parent::`, `ancestor::`): a class chain can only go down, so most of the skips are these.
- **Position on a step, not on the whole result**:
  - `//X[2]`, `//X[last()]`, `X[pred][1]` and `child::*[1]` pick the n-th child of each parent. A class chain index counts across the whole result set, so these would select different elements.
  - `(//X[...])[n]` is fine and is converted.
- **Positions a class chain can't express**: ranges like `position() <= 2`, and an inner index inside a global one (x112, x378, x492).
- **Unions that aren't a single path**: x058, x256, x279, x539, x653. Unions of simple `//*[...]` predicates are converted as `OR`.
- **Locators that can't match anything in the XCUITest tree**:
  - `text()`, `.` and `@text`.
  - `XCUIElementTypeAny` and `XCUIElementTypeLabel`.
- **No equivalent in a class chain predicate**: tokenize, string-join, replace, normalize-space, string-length, count, numeric comparisons on `@x` and `@value`, and child-only existence tests.
- **Broken or unsafe to convert**:
  - x091 and x530 aren't valid XPath.
  - x334 has a literal backtick in the value, which is the class chain predicate delimiter, and I couldn't confirm a safe way to escape it.

## Judgment calls you may want to check
- **Class chain index**: `(//X[p])[n]` becomes ``**/X[`p`][n]`` (and `[last()]` becomes `[-1]`). This assumes WDA counts the index over the whole result in document order, which is my understanding of its behaviour but I haven't confirmed it.
- **Descendant tests**: `.//` and `descendant::` conditions use the `$…$` descendant predicate (x092, x238, x251, x604, x620). I treat that predicate as matching any descendant, not just direct children.
- **XPath 2.0 functions**: `ends-with`, `lower-case`, `upper-case` and `matches` (x288, x400, x443, x595, x607, x676) are converted by intent. WDA's XPath 1.0 engine would reject the originals.
- **x294**: `@enabled=true()` is true for every Button under strict XPath 1.0, since the attribute always exists. I converted it as `enabled == true`.
- **Missing attributes**: x365 (`@label!="a"`) becomes `label != nil AND label != "a"`, because XPath is false when the attribute is missing.
- **x105**: the inner `[1]` is collapsed, since the first of the first children is just the first child overall.
- **Special characters**:
  - x651 (`C:\dir`) has its backslash doubled.
  - x330, x484 and x575 keep a literal newline inside the string.
- **Absolute paths** (x467, x654): I dropped `XCUIElementTypeApplication`, because a class chain already starts at the app.
- **Type tests**: `contains(@type, "XCUIElementTypeX")` and `@type="X"` became a typed step (`**/XCUIElementTypeX`) instead of a `type` predicate.
